# TODO.md — the persistent source of truth

This file is how work resumes after a context compaction, a restart, or a new
agent. Tick items as they finish. Add categories as plans land. If a task is not
here, add it and tick it. Implementation details do not belong here — only tasks
worth tracking.

Legend: `[ ]` pending · `[~]` in progress · `[x]` done · `[!]` blocked · `[-]` cancelled

### Design tokens and theming (`tokens-theme`)

`[x]` `[██████████]` 141/141

`[x]` Measure the **label an accent row paints** — `NavigationMenuLink`'s hover and a highlighted `MentionInputItem` both fill their row `accent` and paint the label `accentForeground`, so those are row labels rather than the on-colour of a filled control; every other row label (`popoverForeground` on the `hover`/`active` wash, `selectedForeground` on the washes a list row wears) is held to the body floor, while this pair was held at the secondary floor, so a brand whose accent foreground measured 4.68:1 passed the gate with a navigation or suggestion label under the page's reading floor. The pair is measured at the body floor now, and **the change found the two macOS styles**: light read 6.53:1 and dark 6.74:1, so their `accentForeground` takes the smallest step that clears (`#09457F`, `#B2D3F9`); every other shipped, high-contrast, platform and authored style already cleared it, and the tightest placement is Light · macOS at 7.19:1. The darker accent label also moves the filled accent face's pre-clamp press ratio from 4.13:1 to 4.42:1 (still under 4.5), so macOS dark now clamps at 17% like the two high-contrast themes; the three action fills and every shipped action are unchanged. `contrast.test.ts` gains `the label an accent row paints` (4 cases): the pair's floor, both painters, a 4.68:1 brand the old floor passed, and the 16-style sweep with the printed value; the catalogue and design-system rows are read there. `styles.test.ts`'s clamp case follows the moved ratio and step. Directions measured: before the change the floor, brand and sweep cases fail by name; after it the tokens suite is green (37 files / 2 347 tests). Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Contrast/§Action fills, `docs/design-system.md` §8/§9, the package README and the `Action fills` row.

`[x]` Ship the **syntax palette** a native `<code>` host highlights with — `@gpuix/native@0.11.0` reads token colours from the theme object's `syntax` field and falls back to its own palette designed for its dark default, and this package shipped none, so a light theme's code block was highlighted for a dark canvas while `docs/tokens.md` recorded "highlighting stays a consumer's decision". `syntaxColors(theme)` resolves **twenty-four** token types (`syntaxRoles`, every key the pinned `SyntaxTheme` reads) from four authored tables — `lightSyntax`, `darkSyntax` and a high-contrast pair — by mode and contrast variant. A token that names code is held to the **body floor** on both fills a host paints (`syntaxSurfaces` = `input` and the page role a code block fills, the two `nativeTextFills`); a `comment` — an annotation about the code rather than the code — to the **secondary floor**, which a high-contrast theme raises to 7:1, and that is the only difference between the default and high-contrast tables. `syntaxFailures(theme, floors?)` reports every token, fill and ratio and reports a colour it cannot measure; `auditTheme` folds it in as `audit.syntax`, so the gate has **eleven** reports and `passed` reads it. A theme owns a palette by carrying `syntax`, which **replaces the table whole** (a complete palette is what the host reads; a brand spreads `syntaxColors(theme)` to edit one token — `Partial<Record<…>>` cannot accept an object literal here because TypeScript's inherited `Object.constructor` collides with the runtime's `constructor` token), and a `PlatformStyle` may declare one per mode, which `applyStyle` hands over under its palette rule. **Adopted with no component change**: the components package's `CodeBlock` passes `nativeTextTheme(theme, "background")`, and the seam now hands `syntaxColors(theme)` to the host. `syntax.test.ts` (12 cases) holds the tables, the 672-placement sweep over the 14 shipped, platform and look themes, the tightest cell (dark `keyword` on Linux's page, **7.22:1**), the resolution, the brand and style routes, the erased keyword, the unmeasurable `hsl()` token and the executed example; `catalogue-values.test.ts` holds the printed table (24 rows × two columns), the four table names, the two high-contrast comment values and the printed tightest to the exports. Directions measured: removing `syntax: syntaxColors(theme)` fails three cases by name in `syntax.test.ts`/`native-text.test.ts`, dropping the `syntax` half of `passed` fails `reports a token that vanishes into the page`, painting the light `keyword` as the page fails the sweep and the printed row, and a printed `#3B2C91` fails the catalogue case. Docs: `docs/tokens.md` §Syntax palette (table, floors, brand and look routes, the retracted limitation), `docs/design-system.md` §9, the package README and the **Syntax palette** inventory row. The painted pixels are the interlock below

`[x]` Measure the **brand link on a message's own tint** — `brandText(theme)` derives one colour for the eight surfaces a link can sit on, and a status tint is not one of them: an `Alert`'s description is a container (`alert.tsx`: "It is a container, so it may hold an action") filled with the tone's `xSoft` role, and a `link` action inside it paints `text-brand` → `brandText` (`packages/primitives/src/recipe/registry.ts`). Measured, that shared colour is under the text floor in **29 of the 64** tint placements across the sixteen shipped, high-contrast, platform and authored styles — macOS dark **3.43:1** on `warningSoft`, where the raw fill role is 2.32:1; the base light theme's 4.46:1 on `infoSoft` and the base dark theme's 3.94:1 on `warningSoft` are two more — and no single colour can fix that without dragging every link on the page away from the brand, because a tint is one tone from the page. So `brandTextOn(theme, surface, floors?)` holds the same 2% derivation (brand where the surface carries it, otherwise the smallest step toward `foreground`, never past it, an unmeasurable value returned unchanged) to **one** role: it clears every one of the 64 placements. The message's own copy stays `statusTone(theme, tone).foreground`, measured on the tint at the body floor. `brand-text.test.ts` gains eight cases — the painters (the alert tones, the container sentence and the registry's `text-brand`), the 29/64 measurement with macOS dark's two values and the base themes by name, the 16 × 4 sweep, kept-vs-stepped on both base themes, the high-contrast floor (High contrast light's 5.81:1 on `infoSoft` steps to 7:1), the unmeasurable brand, and the executed `messageLinkStyles` — plus the page case that prints the count and both macOS cells from the same computation. `brand-text.example.ts` gains `messageLinkStyles`, and `docs/tokens.md` §Brand text gains §A brand run inside a message, `docs/design-system.md` §3 the rule, the README the helper and the `Brand text` row both. `[x]` Paint a surface whose theme **lost an elevation level** instead of throwing — the newest absence rule says a theme stored by an older release is one audit line rather than a crash (`invalidColorRoles`, `invalidShadowColors`, the pair contracts), and `invalidShadowColors` names a missing level once at position `0` with `color: undefined`. The **paint** path did not keep that promise: `elevationShadow(theme, level)` read `theme.elevation[level][0]` directly, so the first raised card, popover or dialog on that theme threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')` — the exception landing where the report had just explained the absence, and on a desktop window taking the surface with it. The helper now takes `{ readonly elevation: Partial<Elevation> }` (the shape `invalidShadowColors` already accepts) and reads `?.[0]`, so an absent level resolves to `undefined` — the same flat surface as the reserved empty `overlay` — while a complete theme is unchanged and the gate keeps reporting the level. `incomplete.test.ts` gains two cases: a stored light theme missing `md` resolves `md` to `undefined` while `sm` and `lg` stay the shipped shadows, and every level of all 16 shipped, high-contrast, platform and authored styles is dropped in turn with the absent level painting nothing and every survivor still the theme's own. Directions measured: at `HEAD` both cases fail with the exact `TypeError … (reading '0')` at `elevationShadow` (`src/incomplete.test.ts:209`), and with the guard they pass alongside the 2 144 existing tests. Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Elevation and `docs/design-system.md` §7/§9 now state that the paint follows the same absence rule as the report.

`[x]` Refuse a theme that **lost a numeric group** instead of failing with a `TypeError` — `auditTheme`'s JSDoc promised "an incomplete theme does not crash the gate", and `docs/tokens.md`/`docs/design-system.md` went further: a missing numeric group was "read as the groups a theme carries". It was not: `invalidNumbers` opened `theme.typography` (and every other group) directly, so a theme stored by a release that predates a group — the one way a complete theme becomes incomplete — reached the consumer as `TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object`, naming neither the group nor the release. The reports cannot describe that absence (the components read every step in a group and a group is a breaking change, not an additive one), so the gate now **refuses** it up front with an actionable message (`a theme must carry every numeric group: \`typography\` is missing. … must be rebuilt from a shipped one with \`extendTheme\`.`), while the additive absences it already handles — a colour role, an elevation level — still come back as a failing report rather than a throw. `incomplete.test.ts` gains `an absent numeric group` (3 cases): each of the six groups refused by name, two groups named at once, and a theme missing only a role and a level still returning an audit with `passed: false`. Directions measured: deleting the `requireGroups` call fails the first two by name, and the additive case holds the other half. Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Paint-ready values and `docs/design-system.md` §9 now state the refusal and quote the message.

The contracts that measure a pair take the same colour source — `contrastFailures`, `decorativeFailures`, `indicatorFailures`, `seriesFailures`, `disabledFadeFailures`, `keyboardDimFailures`, `selectionFailures` (whose `wash` may now be absent) and `fadedPair` — and a pair they cannot compose is reported **unmeasurable** rather than skipped, so `auditTheme` names the missing role and fails `passed` instead of throwing; `NumberSource` reads the levels a theme carries, because a numeric group is a breaking change while a role is additive. `incomplete.test.ts` (8 cases) removes every role and every elevation level from all 16 shipped, high-contrast, platform and authored themes and asserts the gate names it, the pairs touching it stay unmeasurable, and nothing throws; it also holds the total paint check, the documentation order, the single-role case and a complete theme still passing. `[x]` Measure the **ring on the fill it hugs** — `contrastPairs` held the ring to the strips a control *rests* on (page, card, popover, `muted`, `secondary`) and to nothing the same element paints behind itself: `list.tsx` fills `selected`, tints `accent` while hovered and `active` while pressed, and declares the keyboard ring on that row; a ghost or outline action tints the same two washes under its ring; and a field's ring borders the field's own `input` fill, which is not the page it sits on. `outlineOffset: 0` draws the line on the border box, so its inner side touches the fill and its outer side the strip behind it, and a ring that matches the row it surrounds is a focus state nobody sees. Five pairs joined `contrastPairs` (69 → 74) at `contrastFloors.boundary`: `ring` on `input`, `selected`, `hover`, `active` and `accent`. **It found the documented house theme**: its dark ring `#8A6EFF` sat at **2.96:1** on its own `selected` wash (`#3E317E`), so a focused selected row painted its focus line in the row's colour; the ring is now the light violet `#9B8CFF` (3.90:1 there, and it clears the floor on all five fills), which is also the value the other documented brand already used. Every shipped, high-contrast, platform and authored theme clears its variant's floor, the tightest being the base light theme's pressed wash at **3.04:1** — recorded rather than widened, because the ring is a 2px line on a state the reader's own pointer created. `contrast.test.ts`'s `the ring on the fill it hugs` suite reads both painters (so the pairs cannot outlive the paint), reports a ring painted the selected fill and one the pressed wash hides at 1.00:1, and sweeps all 16 styles while holding the catalogue's printed 3.04 to the same computation. Directions measured: removing one pair fails the coverage case, the erased-ring case and the printed count by name; a stale printed `3.05` fails the sweep case; reverting the house ring fails `platforms.test.ts`'s both-modes case. Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Contrast, `docs/design-system.md` §9, the package README's platform snippet and the `Contrast contract` inventory row.

`[x]` Measure the **fully opaque alpha byte** a theme can write — `alpha(color, 1)` is the package's own helper and returns `#RRGGBBFF`; the renderer paints it and `invalidColorRoles` accepts it, while `src/hex.ts` read any alpha byte as a share, so **every pair a role written that way touched** was reported unmeasurable and the gate failed a palette it passes in six digits — the same false-failure class as the shorthand, one form further on. An `FF` byte is no share, so `measuredHex` now reports no alpha for it and the colour measures as its six-digit twin (any byte below `FF` still marks a translucent value; `alphaOf` still reads `1`, and `blend` now returns the measurable six-digit form for an opaque base instead of carrying an opaque byte forward). `color.test.ts`'s `the hex dialect the contracts measure` gains `measures a fully opaque alpha byte` (long, bare, 4-digit and `alpha(..., 1)` forms through `contrastRatio`, `alphaOf` and `blend`), and `audit.test.ts` gains `a brand whose colours carry a fully opaque alpha byte`, which rewrites every opaque role of the high-contrast light palette through `alpha(..., 1)` (leaving the three designed shares — `selection`, `overlay`, `shadow` — alone) and proves the audit's contrast report is empty and `passed` matches the six-digit theme's. Three directions measured: before the fix the dialect case and both audit cases fail (`expected undefined to be close to 21`, `passed` false), and the fix leaves 1628 tokens tests green. Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §`alpha`/§`alphaOf`/§Paint-ready values/§Limitations, `docs/design-system.md` §9, the package README and the `Colour grammar` row

`[x]` Measure whether a **control's box fits the text it carries** — a control is built at exactly `density.controlHeight[size]` and lays its text at a type role's leading (`controlStyle` uses `label`, `fieldTextStyle` uses `body` in `packages/primitives/src/core/style.ts`), and no contract compared the two: `invalidNumbers` asked that each number be finite and that a control height be pressable, so `extendTheme(lightTheme, { density: "compact", typography: { body: { lineHeight: 26 } } })` passed every report while the label was two pixels taller than its 24px `sm` box and would spill or clip. `NumberRule` gains `fits` — the second rule about two tokens and the only one across two groups — applied where the height is inspected: every `controlHeight` size must reach the taller of `label`'s and `body`'s leading, reported on the height that has to grow. A box exactly equal to the leading passes (the line fills it), a height already under `pressable` is reported once by that floor rather than twice, and an unusable leading stays the type report's. `auditTheme.passed` reads it through the existing `invalidNumbers` report, so no gate shape or docs-site readout changed. `numbers.test.ts` (40 cases) holds all 16 shipped, platform and authored themes to an empty report, proves both roles and both directions (a 26px body and a 26px label each outgrow only `compact` `sm`, an exact 24px leading passes), the single-report rule for a shrunken box and a `NaN` leading, the preset sweep and a brand whose only defect is the fit; `numbers.example.ts` gains `tallTypeTheme`/`tallTypeAudit` as the fourth documented brand. Directions measured: with `fits` disabled four cases fail by name (both role cases, the gate case and the catalogue's real-report case), deleting the catalogue row fails it again, and dropping the design-system sentence fails the prose case; the fix leaves 1636 tokens tests green. Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Numbers, `docs/design-system.md` §6/§9, the package README and the `Token numbers` row

`[x]` Measure the **shadow a raised surface drops** — the one surface both pages said was *deliberately* outside the contract ("a shadow is a blurred geometry, so a flat composite would overstate it"), and the exemption hid a real defect: the high-contrast dark theme tints its shadows with black (`highContrastDarkColors.shadow` was `#000000B3`) on a **pure-black page**, so every level measured 1.00:1 on `background` and a dialog or a full-width card in that variant had no shadow at all. **Decision: measure it as a ceiling.** `DecorativeSurface` gains `surface: "elevation"` with a `level`, the painted colour is the **level's own** (a level carries its share in its alpha byte, and a brand can supply one whole), and the table measures the scale's **deepest** step (`lg`) over the four strips a raised surface falls on (`background`, `card`, `popover`, `muted`) at `decorativeFloor`. Overstating in the safe direction is the point: a shadow that passes may still read faint at its blurred edge, and only one a reader cannot see at all is reported. It rides the existing `decorative` report, so **no new `ThemeAudit` key, no count word on `/docs/themes` and no docs-site change** — the editor's `formatDecorativeFailure` words it as `elevation: shadow on background — 1.00:1 (needs 1.05:1)` already. The high-contrast dark `shadow` is the grey its raised controls use (`#2E2E2EB3`), and the deepest level now reads 1.21–1.37:1 on all four strips (its `sm`/`md` read 1.09–1.39 too). `decorative.test.ts` (31 cases) holds the four placements, a caller-supplied level whose colour is transparent while the role is perfect (so the report reads the level and not the role), the pre-fix high-contrast dark theme by name (`1.00` on `background`, the only strip it erased), a brand whose `shadow` is its page, an absent level as unmeasurable, the authored looks, and the executed `flatShadowBrand` example; `coverage.test.ts`'s `shadow` exemption is gone (the role is a placement now), `elevation.test.ts` and `catalogue-values.test.ts` move to the new painted cells. Directions measured: reverting the tint fails `reports the high-contrast dark page no level could lift` and `passes every shipped theme`, and dropping the placements fails seven cases by name, the coverage case naming `shadow` first. Docs in `docs/tokens.md` §Decorative surfaces/§Elevation/§Every role is measured, `docs/design-system.md` §5/§7/§9, the package README and the `Elevation`/`Contrast contract` inventory rows

`[x]` Measure the **face a disabled control wears** — the disabled state's contract measured its **label** (`disabledForeground` on `disabled`, on the page surfaces and the group strips) and `disabledAction(theme)` replaced the rejected fade with that pair, but the **fill** was measured by nothing: a disabled control does not sit on a strip, it *replaces* an enabled control, so an unavailable action that wears the enabled one's fill tells the reader it can be pressed. The quiet step is `#F2F2F2` / `#1A1A1A` now (both clear all five, and the disabled label rises to 6.16:1 / 5.04:1 in the high-contrast pair). **The strip behind the control is deliberately not measured**, and that is recorded rather than implied: `disabled` *is* the base light theme's `muted` (1.00:1), the base dark theme's is its `popover` and toolbar, and both high-contrast variants' is their `muted` — a quiet fill on a quiet strip is the design, while a quiet fill on an enabled face is the defect. `decorative.test.ts` gains `measures a disabled face against every available face it replaces` and `reports a disabled action painted in the enabled action's face` (a brand whose `disabled` is its `secondary` reports `1.00:1`), the pre-fix high-contrast pair by name (`secondary` 1.00 and `accent` 1.03), and `decorative.example.ts`'s `unavailableActionBrand` reports `disabledFace: disabled on secondary is 1.00`; the shipped/platform/look sweeps hold all 16 styles. `[x]` `@gpuixui/motion`: **an unreadable clock reached the formulas**. Every sampler was written to be total — `springPhysics` falls back from unusable physics, `MotionValue.sample` holds its last frame for a clock it cannot read, and `sampleSpring`'s own JSDoc promises "non-finite inputs are sanitized" — but `sampleSpring`, `sampleInertia`, `sampleKeyframes` and `Sequence.sample` all computed `Math.max(elapsedMs, 0)`, which is `NaN` for a `NaN` clock: a spring returned the **target** as a settled first frame, an inertia coast and a keyframe run returned `NaN` (the runtime paints a `NaN` inset as nothing), and `Sequence.complete(NaN)` stayed false forever. A tween was worse: `tween(NaN)` divided the clock into `NaN`, so `MotionValue` wrote a `NaN` value, never finished and churned a frame every 16 ms for the life of the tree (`tween(Infinity)` never finished either), which is exactly the class of unusable duration the package already refuses in its physics and the components refuse in their reveal/delay helpers. The samplers now read a `NaN` clock (or progress) as the start of the run and still clamp an infinity to the end, and a tween duration that cannot run falls back to the house `DEFAULT_TWEEN_MS` (300 ms) in one helper the declared transition and `MotionValue.advance` share, so a re-declared `tween(NaN)` also compares equal. Proof: five new cases in `motion.test.ts`, `spring.test.ts`, `inertia.test.ts` and `timeline.test.ts` — each measured failing at `HEAD` with the exact payload (`expected NaN to be 300`, `expected { value: NaN, velocity: NaN }`, `expected { value: 1 } to deeply equal { value: +0 }`, `expected NaN to be 10`, `expected [ { state: 'active', value: NaN } ]`), green after (55/55; `check-types`, lint, `check:tests` clean). Docs: `packages/motion/README.md` §Inputs the runtime can paint and the two sampler JSDocs.
`[x]` `@gpuixui/motion`: the **retarget rule that keeps a run from restarting** was unmeasured. `motion.ts`'s `animate` returns early for "identical declarations" and the README promises `transitionEquals` "compares them structurally so a re-declared transition does not restart a run", but neither the helper nor the no-op had a case: a regression there would re-arm a 100 ms tween on every render (its start moves to the latest sample), so a surface repainting at frame rate crawled toward its target and never completed while every existing suite stayed green. `motion.test.ts` now pins the helper (instant/tween/spring, duration, easing and each physics field) and the rule both ways — a re-declared `tween(100, linear)` leaves the run at 0.5 and completes at 100, while a slower `tween(200, linear)` restarts from the 0.5 on screen and reaches 0.75 at +100 ms. Directions measured: deleting the early return fails `does not restart a run for a re-declared transition` (`expected 0.75 to be 1`), and making `transitionEquals` answer `true` fails the restart case plus both comparison cases (`expected true to be false`).
